details:
## Summary

On an AMD Radeon RX 6650 XT, with VRChat's Anti-Aliasing set to x2 (MSAA), using a world

mirror causes props that display a RenderTexture (screens / video players / custom-shader

props) to render corrupted: a black center with multi-colored (red / yellow / blue / green)

flickering bands around the edges. The corruption persists after leaving the mirror, and

clears only when the player looks away from the affected prop and back. VRChat's in-game

camera captures the same props CORRECTLY while the main view is corrupted. Setting

Anti-Aliasing to Off completely resolves the issue.

## Environment

- VRChat Build: 2026.3.3-1919-27c41b24d2-Release

- Unity Version: 6000.0.67f1-DWR

- Graphics API: Direct3D 11.0 [level 11.1]

- GPU: AMD Radeon RX 6650 XT (RDNA2 / Navi 23), 8 GB VRAM

- Driver: AMD Software Adrenalin Edition 26.9.2, driver 32.0.21045.11001 (2026-09-25)

- OS: Windows 11 Pro, build 26200

- Display: 1920x1080 @ 180 Hz

- World where reproduced: wrld_0f204305-922c-4548-9008-12d4ac2d1da6

- VRChat Graphics Settings: Quality = Low, Anti-Aliasing = x2 (reproduces) / Off (fixed)

- Launch options: none relevant (issue reproduces without any launch options)

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Set Settings -> Graphics -> Anti-Aliasing to x2 (MSAA).

2. Join a world that contains a mirror (VRC_MirrorReflection) and at least one prop that

   displays a RenderTexture (e.g. a screen or video player).

3. Open / look into the mirror and observe the scene through it.

4. Exit the mirror view and look at the RenderTexture-based prop.

## Actual Result

- The prop renders with a solid black center and multi-colored (red / yellow / blue / green)

  flickering bands around its edges.

- The colors shift as the camera rotates.

- The corruption persists even when no longer looking through the mirror.

- Looking away from the prop until it leaves the view, then looking back at it, restores

  correct rendering.

- VRChat's in-game camera renders the same prop CORRECTLY while the main view is corrupted.

## Expected Result

Props should continue to render normally after using a mirror.

## Workaround

Set Settings -> Graphics -> Anti-Aliasing to **Off**. With MSAA disabled the corruption no

longer reproduces. Reducing the mirror resolution or avoiding the mirror also prevents it.

## Log Evidence

Warning - 'R8_SRGB' is not supported. RenderTexture::GetTemporary fallbacks to R8G8B8A8_SRGB format on this platform. Use 'SystemInfo.IsFormatSupported' C# API to check format support.

at VRC.SDKBase.VRC_MirrorReflection.RenderMirror (UnityEngine.RenderTexture targetTexture, UnityEngine.Vector3 camPosition, UnityEngine.Quaternion camRotation, UnityEngine.Matrix4x4 camProjectionMatrix) at VRC.SDKBase.VRC_MirrorReflection.RenderMirrorCameras (UnityEngine.Camera currentCamera, VRC.SDKBase.VRC_MirrorReflection+ActiveRenderModes visibility) at UnityEngine.Experimental.Rendering.ScriptableRuntimeReflectionSystemWrapper .Internal_ScriptableRuntimeReflectionSystemWrapper_TickRealtimeProbes (System.Boolean& result)

## Hypothesis

`RenderTexture::GetTemporary` is Unity's pooled temporary render texture. The mirror and

RenderTexture-based props draw from the same pool. On this AMD configuration `R8_SRGB` is

reported as unsupported and Unity falls back to `R8G8B8A8_SRGB`. Combined with the extra

MSAA resolve pass performed by the mirror's render texture, the pooled RT appears to be

handed back with a mismatched format / stale binding state, so props that sample a

RenderTexture receive scrambled channels (black center + rainbow banding). The in-game

camera being unaffected indicates per-camera render state pollution rather than asset or

shader compilation corruption. Disabling MSAA removes the resolve pass and the issue.

## Attachments

Two screenshots taken 2026-10-04 08:48 (local time) while the bug was active on the same prop.
title: RenderTexture-based props render corrupted (black center + rainbow edge flicker) after using a mirror when MSAA anti-aliasing is enabled — AMD RDNA2 / Unity 6
